newsitem.title: MALTA: Quiet trading on Malta exchange.
newsitem.headline: Quiet trading on Malta exchange.

text.p: Business was quiet in the once-weekly trading session of the Malta Stock Exchange on Wednesday, with turnover dropping to 458,000 Maltese Lira ($1.2 million) from the previous week's 3.6 million Maltese Lira.
Business on Wednesday was spread over 88 deals, of which 40 were in equities and 48 in fixed income securities. The share index climbed slightly to 985.62 from last week's 985.34.

Business in equities amounted to just over 35,120 Maltese Lira, with 32,516 shares being transacted. Of these, 16,138 were Bank of Valletta shares, transacted in 20 deals for an average 123 cents, down 1.4 cents.
There were six deals in Mid-Med Bank with 3,283 shares selling for an average 148.7 cents each, up seven mils.
Five deals were struck in Middle Sea Insurance with 4,699 shares selling for an average 120.6 cents, down six mils.

Dealings in Simonds Farsons Cisk saw 7,455 ordinary shares changing hands for an average price of 50 cents per share, unchanged. In the 8.5 percent Farsons preference shares 1996/99, 941 shares were sold for an average 100.7 cents in four deals, up seven mils.
There were dealings in 11 issues in the government bond market, turnover reaching just over 404,000 Maltese Lira. Business was mainly in the 7.25 percent 2006 and the 7.25 percent MGS 2006 (III).

In corporate bonds, there were four deals in the 6.5 percent Gasan Bonds 1998/99 amounting to 7,392 Maltese Lira. There were 14 deals in Mid-Med Bank 7.25 percent unsecured loan stock 2005, amounting to 12,065 Maltese Lira.
